# linrad

**SM5BSZ's DSP receiver — the deep-toolbox SDR for weak-signal work**

- **Version recorded:** 05.02
- **Categories:** `sdr-receivers`
- **Upstream:** <http://www.sm5bsz.com/linuxdsp/linrad.htm>

## What it does

A software-defined receiver with an unusually deep DSP toolbox — adaptive noise blanking, smart filtering, coherent averaging — driven from a dense X11 interface. The classic choice for EME and other weak-signal work where its blanker still outclasses newer SDR GUIs.

## Why you would want it

Nothing else in the catalog has Linrad's noise-blanking pedigree. If your problem is hearing a station under local impulse noise or off the Moon, this is the tool the weak-signal community still reaches for.

## Before it will work

An SDR or soundcard input, and patience with the interface — first-run setup walks through hardware configuration in a terminal-style UI. Runs under X11; install as `linrad` from the PATH.

## Install and launch

- **Installed by name only** — it is in no profile.
- **Install:** `hammunition install linrad --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Commands it leaves on your PATH: `linrad`.
- **The install needs the network to:** the upstream files the plan lists, each checked against a pinned digest (or, for map and reference data, the publisher or a LAN mirror).

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- source (autotools) from https://www.sm5bsz.com/linuxdsp/archive/lir05-02.tbz — *arch x86_64*
  - build dependencies: `build-essential`, `patch`, `nasm`, `libx11-dev`, `libxext-dev`
  - the project's build system has no install rule; the binaries listed below are copied into the prefix instead
  - Patched before configure runs, so the generated Makefile inherits the fix. The 64-bit X11 target (xlinrad64) is what AHRL shipped; the ARM targets are unmeasured here and the block is x86_64-gated rather than guessed (D-002, D-025).

Binaries this produces:

- `xlinrad64` → `linrad`

## Known problems

The interface predates every modern UI convention; read SM5BSZ's site before judging it. Built with -Werror removed (see the patch) — the warnings are real but benign 1990s C, and fixing them upstream is beyond a packaging project's remit.

## Keeping it current

- probe: none
- strategy: rebuild
- Upstream versions land as lirNN-MM.tbz in sm5bsz.com/linuxdsp/archive/. Slow-moving and worth checking manually; the SourceForge mirror carries only packaged snapshots.

Leif Asbrink SM5BSZ's site and the linrad mailing list — documentation is extensive, in its own idiom.
